question: The term ‘Back-stick’ is used in which of the following games/sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Backstick" (or "back-stick") is a foul in hockey, awarded against a player who strikes or plays the ball with the rounded/reverse back side of the stick instead of the flat playing side. (बैक-स्टिक — हॉकी)

 

• Under hockey's stick-handling rules, a player is permitted to play the ball only with the flat face of the stick; using the rounded back is illegal and results in a foul/free hit to the opposing team.

 

• Hockey has many such specialised terms for fouls and techniques — e.g. obstruction, sticks, and undercutting — that describe legal and illegal ways of using the stick.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's National Game (traditionally regarded as such) is Hockey; the Indian men's hockey team has won 8 Olympic gold medals, the most by any country.

 

• Other stick-and-ball sports include ice hockey, polo, and hurling, but the term "back-stick" specifically belongs to field hockey's rulebook.

 

NOTE

 

• Basketball (Option 1): Uses terms like travelling, double dribble, and goaltending; sticks are not used in this sport.

 

• Badminton (Option 2): Uses a racquet, not a stick; terms include let, fault, and smash.

 

• Volleyball (Option 4): Played with hands/arms over a net; terms include double touch, carry, and rotation fault — no stick is involved.

question: Which of the following festivals in Punjab is celebrated to commemorate the formation of the Khalsa Panth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baisakhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baisakhi (Vaisakhi) is celebrated on 13/14 April every year and commemorates the founding of the Khalsa Panth by the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, on 13 April 1699 at Anandpur Sahib. (बैसाखी — खालसा पंथ की स्थापना)

 

• On this day, Guru Gobind Singh initiated the Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) and formally established the Khalsa as a collective body of baptised Sikhs bound by a common code of conduct (Rehat).

 

• Baisakhi is also celebrated as a harvest festival across Punjab and North India, marking the ripening of the rabi crop.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hola Mohalla is a Sikh festival held a day after Holi at Anandpur Sahib, featuring mock battles and martial displays, started by Guru Gobind Singh.

 

• Baisakhi is also New Year's Day in the traditional Punjabi (Bikrami) calendar and is celebrated under different names across India, such as Vishu (Kerala) and Pohela Boishakh (Bengal).

 

NOTE

 

• Lohri (Option 1): A winter folk festival of Punjab marking the end of winter, celebrated around 13 January with bonfires.

 

• Hola Mohalla (Option 2): A Sikh martial festival held near Holi, not linked to the founding of the Khalsa.

 

• Teej (Option 3): A monsoon festival celebrated by women, associated with the worship of Goddess Parvati, unrelated to the Khalsa Panth.

question: What theme was decided to celebrate the second ‘International Day of Yoga’ in India?
option_1: Yoga for the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yoga for the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2nd International Day of Yoga, observed on 21 June 2016, had the theme "Yoga for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals", linking the practice of yoga to broader goals of health and sustainable living. (अंतरराष्ट्रीय योग दिवस — सतत विकास लक्ष्य)

 

• The International Day of Yoga was first proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his UN General Assembly address in September 2014, and the UN declared 21 June as IDY through a resolution adopted on 11 December 2014.

 

• The 1st International Day of Yoga (2015) was celebrated with the theme "Yoga for Harmony and Peace", and the main event was held at Rajpath, New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• June 21 was chosen as it is the Summer Solstice, the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, considered significant in many cultures.

 

• Subsequent IDY themes include "Yoga for Health" (2017), "Yoga for Peace" (2018), "Climate Action" (2019), and "Yoga at Home and Yoga with Family" (2020).

 

NOTE

 

• Yoga for Peace (Option 2): This was closer to the 2018 IDY theme, not the second edition.

 

• Yoga for Wellness (Option 3): Not an official IDY theme for the second edition.

 

• Yoga for Heart (Option 4): Not an official IDY theme; heart-health awareness is a general benefit associated with yoga but was not the 2016 theme.

question: Chemical formula of quick lime is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaO.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Quick lime, also known as calcium oxide (CaO), is produced by heating (calcining) limestone (CaCO3) at high temperature, releasing carbon dioxide. (बुझा न चूना/क्विक लाइम — कैल्शियम ऑक्साइड)

 

• The reaction is: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 (thermal decomposition).

 

• Quick lime reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime (calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2), releasing a large amount of heat: CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Quick lime is widely used in the manufacture of cement, in whitewashing, in the leather industry, and in steel manufacturing as a flux.

 

• Slaked lime, Ca(OH)2, is used to make bleaching powder and in lime mortar for construction.

 

NOTE

 

• CO2 (Option 2): Carbon dioxide — a gas released during the calcination of limestone, not quick lime itself.

 

• CaCO3 (Option 3): Calcium carbonate — this is limestone/marble, the raw material used to produce quick lime, not quick lime itself.

 

• Ca(OH)2 (Option 4): Calcium hydroxide — this is slaked lime, formed when quick lime reacts with water, not quick lime itself.

question: What is the unit of work done?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SI unit of work done is the Joule (J), named after physicist James Prescott Joule. (जूल — कार्य की इकाई)

 

• Work done = Force × Displacement, and since Force is measured in Newtons (N) and displacement in metres (m), one Joule is equivalent to 1 Newton-metre (N·m).

 

• Since Energy is the capacity to do work, the Joule is also the SI unit of energy (in all its forms — kinetic, potential, heat, etc.).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Power (rate of doing work) is measured in Watt (W), where 1 Watt = 1 Joule/second.

 

• Other common energy units include the calorie (1 cal ≈ 4.18 J) and the kilowatt-hour (kWh), used for electrical energy billing.

 

NOTE

 

• Watt (Option 1): This is the unit of power, not work — the rate at which work is done.

 

• Decibel (Option 2): This is the unit used to measure sound intensity/loudness.

 

• Ampere (Option 3): This is the SI unit of electric current.

question: Which of the following sites do “Not” have nuclear power plant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijayawada.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh) does not host a nuclear power plant; it is not among India's operational nuclear power station sites. (विजयवाड़ा — कोई परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र नहीं)

 

• Narora Atomic Power Station is located in Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Ganga.

 

• Tarapur Atomic Power Station in Maharashtra was India's first nuclear power plant, commissioned in 1969, while Rawatbhata (Rajasthan Atomic Power Station) in Rajasthan was India's second.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Indian nuclear power stations include Kaiga (Karnataka), Kakrapar (Gujarat), Kalpakkam/MAPS (Tamil Nadu) and Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu).

 

• India's nuclear power programme is operated primarily by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).

 

NOTE

 

• Naraura (Option 2): Has an operational nuclear power plant (NAPS) in Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Tarapur (Option 3): Has an operational nuclear power plant (TAPS) in Maharashtra.

 

• Rawat Bhata (Option 4): Has an operational nuclear power plant (RAPS) in Rajasthan.

question: The Ramakrishna Mission stressed the ideal of __________ through social service and selfless action.
solution_text:
The correct answer is salvation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897 in memory of his guru Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, stressed the ideal of salvation (moksha) through social service and selfless action (seva). (रामकृष्ण मिशन — सेवा द्वारा मोक्ष)

 

• This philosophy is rooted in Practical Vedanta, summed up in the mission's motto "Atmano Mokshartham Jagad-hitaya cha" — "for one's own salvation and for the welfare of the world."

 

• The Mission holds that service to humanity (Daridra Narayana Seva — seeing God in the poor) is itself a form of worship and a path to spiritual liberation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ramakrishna Math and Mission is headquartered at Belur Math, West Bengal, on the banks of the Hooghly river.

 

• Swami Vivekananda famously represented Hinduism at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893.

 

NOTE

 

• bhakti (Option 1): Devotion is a component of many Hindu spiritual paths, but is not the specific ideal emphasised through the Mission's social-service work.

 

• education (Option 2): While the Mission does run schools and colleges, its founding ideal centres on service leading to salvation, not education itself.

 

• God (Option 4): Too generic; the Mission's specific stated purpose links selfless service to personal salvation, not merely "God" as an abstract ideal.

question: International Non-Violence Day is observed on:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 October.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on 2 October every year, marking the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. (अंतरराष्ट्रीय अहिंसा दिवस — 2 अक्टूबर, गांधी जयंती)

 

• It was established by a UN General Assembly resolution in June 2007, to disseminate the message of non-violence through education and public awareness.

 

• The day affirms the relevance of non-violence (Ahimsa) as a principle and a means of securing a culture of peace, tolerance and understanding.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• 2 October is also celebrated in India as Gandhi Jayanti, a national holiday.

 

• Gandhi's philosophy of non-violent resistance (Satyagraha) influenced civil rights movements worldwide, including that of Martin Luther King Jr.

 

NOTE

 

• 15 August (Option 1): India's Independence Day.

 

• 31 October (Option 2): National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas), marking Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.

 

• 14 November (Option 4): Children's Day in India, marking Jawaharlal Nehru's birth anniversary.

question: Which of the following Dynasties established the kingdom of Vijayanagara?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangama Dynasty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 CE by brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, who belonged to the Sangama Dynasty, the first of the four dynasties that ruled Vijayanagara. (संगम वंश — विजयनगर साम्राज्य की स्थापना)

 

• The empire was established on the banks of the Tungabhadra river in present-day Karnataka, with its capital at Vijayanagara (Hampi).

 

• The four ruling dynasties of Vijayanagara, in order, were: Sangama (1336-1485), Saluva (1485-1505), Tuluva (1505-1570) and Aravidu (1570-1646).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The most celebrated Vijayanagara ruler was Krishnadevaraya, who belonged to the Tuluva Dynasty and whose reign (1509-1529) is considered the empire's golden age.

 

• The ruins of Hampi are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagama Dynasty (Option 2): Not a recognised historical dynasty of Vijayanagara; likely a distractor name resembling "Sangama."

 

• Soma Dynasty (Option 3): Not one of the ruling dynasties of Vijayanagara.

 

• Tuluva Dynasty (Option 4): This was the third dynasty to rule Vijayanagara (notably under Krishnadevaraya), not the founding dynasty.

question: When was ‘Vayudoot’ airline setup in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1981.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vayudoot was a regional airline of India, established in 1981 as a joint venture between Indian Airlines and Air India, to connect smaller towns and remote regions not served by the major carriers. (वायुदूत — क्षेत्रीय विमान सेवा, स्थापना 1981)

 

• It primarily operated short-haul flights to the North-East, hill states and other remote areas using smaller aircraft such as the Dornier Do-228.

 

• Vayudoot ceased operations and was merged into Indian Airlines in 1997 due to financial difficulties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vayudoot's role of connecting remote regions is echoed today by the government's UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) regional connectivity scheme.

 

• India's flag carrier at the time, Air India, was nationalised in 1953 along with domestic carriers merged to form Indian Airlines.

 

NOTE

 

• 1991 (Option 2): Incorrect year; this is also the year of India's economic liberalisation, unrelated to Vayudoot's founding.

 

• 1971 (Option 3): Incorrect year for Vayudoot's establishment.

 

• 1969 (Option 4): This is the year Indian Airlines and Air India were nationalised under the Air Corporations Act, not when Vayudoot was set up.

question: Wearing away of landscape by different agents like water, wind and ice is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Erosion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Erosion is the process by which the landscape is worn away and its material transported from one place to another by agents such as water, wind, ice (glaciers) and waves. (अपरदन — भू-दृश्य का घिसाव व परिवहन)

 

• It differs from weathering, which is the in-situ breakdown of rocks (by physical, chemical or biological processes) without significant transport of material.

 

• Erosion shapes major landforms such as river valleys, canyons, sand dunes and coastal cliffs over long periods.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The sequence of processes is typically: weathering → erosion → transportation → deposition (sedimentation).

 

• Glacial erosion creates distinctive landforms such as U-shaped valleys, cirques and moraines.

 

NOTE

 

• Weathering (Option 1): The in-place breakdown/decay of rocks, without necessarily involving movement/transport of the debris.

 

• Metamorphosis (Option 3): A biological/geological term referring to a change in form or structure (e.g., rock metamorphism under heat and pressure), not the wearing away of landscape.

 

• Sedimentation (Option 4): The deposition of eroded material, which is the end result of erosion, not the wearing-away process itself.

question: Who has been appointed as the new chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes in June 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitin Gupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitin Gupta, an IRS (Income Tax) officer of the 1986 batch, took over as Chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) on 27 June 2022. (केंद्रीय प्रत्यक्ष कर बोर्ड — नितिन गुप्ता)

 

• The CBDT is a statutory authority functioning under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963, and is the administrative body for the Income Tax Department, functioning under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

 

• Nitin Gupta's tenure was subsequently extended, and he was later succeeded by Ravi Agrawal as CBDT Chairman in mid-2024.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CBDT's counterpart for indirect taxes is the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).

 

• Both CBDT and CBIC are headed by a Chairman and function under the overall control of the Department of Revenue.

 

NOTE

 

• Nidhi Chibber (Option 2): An IAS officer who has held roles such as Chairperson of CBSE, not CBDT Chairman.

 

• Ashish Jha (Option 3): Not the CBDT Chairman appointed in June 2022.

 

• M Jagadesh Kumar (Option 4): An academic administrator; he was serving as Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) around this period, and later became UGC Chairman, not CBDT Chairman.

question: Who among the following is known as ‘Sarod Samrat’ in Indian Classical Music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amjad Ali Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is popularly known as "Sarod Samrat" (Emperor of the Sarod), a title reflecting his mastery of the sarod, a plucked stringed instrument of Indian classical music. (सरोद सम्राट — उस्ताद अमजद अली खान)

 

• He belongs to the Senia Bangash gharana and is credited with popularising the sarod globally through decades of performance and innovation on the instrument.

 

• He has received India's major civilian honours, including the Padma Vibhushan (2001) and is a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amjad Ali Khan's sons, Amaan Ali Bangash and Ayaan Ali Bangash, are also noted sarod players carrying forward the family tradition.

 

• Other legendary sarod players include Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, often called the founder of modern sarod technique.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Ravishankar Prasad (Option 1): Not a recognised classical musician; this name resembles the Indian politician Ravi Shankar Prasad, distinct from sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

 

• Aamir Ali Khan (Option 2): Not a known title-holder as "Sarod Samrat"; likely a distractor name resembling Amjad Ali Khan.

 

• Kishan Maharaj (Option 4): A legendary tabla player (Banaras gharana), not a sarod player.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the methods of national income estimation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banking method.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• There are three standard methods of estimating national income: the Product (Value Added) Method, the Income Method, and the Expenditure Method. "Banking method" is not a recognised method of national income estimation. (राष्ट्रीय आय आकलन — उत्पाद, आय व व्यय विधि)

 

• The Product Method sums the value added by all producing units in the economy during a year.

 

• The Income Method sums all factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit) earned by factors of production, while the Expenditure Method sums all final expenditures (consumption, investment, government spending, net exports).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, national income estimates are prepared and released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

 

• All three genuine methods should theoretically yield the same value of national income, since output, income and expenditure are three views of the same economic flow.

 

NOTE

 

• Expenditure method (Option 2): A genuine, standard method of national income estimation.

 

• Product method (Option 3): A genuine, standard method of national income estimation.

 

• Income method (Option 4): A genuine, standard method of national income estimation.

question: The term ‘Parliament’ refers to the ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is National legislature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In India, the term 'Parliament' refers to the national (Union) legislature, comprising the President, the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People). (संसद — राष्ट्रीय विधायिका)

 

• Parliament is established under Article 79 of the Constitution of India as the supreme legislative body at the national level.

 

• The Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha are the two Houses of Parliament, but neither alone constitutes "Parliament" — the term denotes the combined national legislative institution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The State legislature, by contrast, is called the State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and, where present, the State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).

 

• The Lok Sabha has a maximum strength of 552 members (as per constitutional provisions), while the Rajya Sabha has a maximum of 250 members.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajya Sabha (Option 1): Only the upper House of Parliament, not the whole institution.

 

• Lok Sabha (Option 2): Only the lower House of Parliament, not the whole institution.

 

• State legislature (Option 3): Refers to a state-level, not national-level, legislative body — a distinct institution from Parliament.

question: Chief Minister of which state has inaugurated a project of the Women and Child Development department to provide milk and eggs to children at all anganwadis in the state in a bid to improve their nutrition levels?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan launched a scheme ("Poshaka Balyam") under the Women and Child Development Department to provide milk and eggs to children at all anganwadis across the state, aimed at improving child nutrition. (केरल — आंगनवाड़ी दूध-अंडा योजना)

 

• The scheme was launched in August 2022, targeting children enrolled in Kerala's anganwadi centres to combat malnutrition and improve health outcomes.

 

• Anganwadi centres, set up under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, are village-level childcare and nutrition centres across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala has consistently ranked high on social development and health indices in India, including low infant mortality and high literacy rates.

 

• The ICDS scheme was launched nationally in 1975 and remains India's flagship programme for early childhood care and nutrition.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): Not the state associated with this particular anganwadi milk-and-eggs initiative.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Not the state associated with this particular initiative.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Not the state associated with this particular initiative (though Tamil Nadu separately runs its own nutrition schemes for anganwadis).

question: A 'Camel Protection and Development Policy' has been announced by the government of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of Rajasthan announced a 'Camel Protection and Development Policy' aimed at conserving the declining camel population in the state through breeding support, subsidies and welfare measures for camel breeders. (ऊंट संरक्षण नीति — राजस्थान)

 

• The camel was declared the State Animal of Rajasthan in 2014, and the Rajasthan Camel (Prohibition of Slaughter and Regulation of Temporary Migration or Export) Act, 2015 was enacted to protect the species.

 

• Rajasthan is home to the majority of India's camel population, particularly in districts like Bikaner, Jaisalmer and Barmer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The annual Pushkar Camel Fair in Rajasthan is one of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs.

 

• Camels in Rajasthan are used for transport, agriculture, tourism and milk production, with camel milk increasingly promoted for its nutritional value.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Not associated with a camel protection policy.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): Also has a camel-rearing tradition (notably the Kharai camel), but the specific 'Camel Protection and Development Policy' referenced belongs to Rajasthan.

 

• Ladakh (Option 4): Known for the double-humped Bactrian camel in Nubra Valley, but not the state associated with this specific policy.

question: Who among the following Presidents of India was also the deputy chairman of Planning Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pranab Mukherjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pranab Mukherjee, who later served as the 13th President of India (2012-2017), earlier served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission of India from 2004 to 2009, before becoming Union Finance Minister. (प्रणब मुखर्जी — योजना आयोग के उपाध्यक्ष)

 

• The Planning Commission (established in 1950, replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015) was headed nominally by the Prime Minister as Chairman, with a Deputy Chairman handling its day-to-day functioning, holding the rank of a Cabinet Minister.

 

• Before becoming President, Pranab Mukherjee had an extensive political career holding portfolios including Finance, External Affairs, and Defence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Planning Commission was responsible for formulating India's Five-Year Plans, a role that NITI Aayog does not perform in the same way.

 

• Pranab Mukherjee was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019.

 

NOTE

 

• V V Giri (Option 1): India's 4th President; was a trade unionist and had earlier served as a state Governor and Union Labour Minister, not Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

 

• K R Narayanan (Option 2): India's 10th President; had a career as a diplomat and Vice-President before becoming President, not Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

 

• Ramaswamy Venkataraman (Option 3): India's 8th President; served as Union Finance and Defence Minister, not Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

question: In Golgi apparatus, the maturing face is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is convex.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Golgi apparatus is a stack of flattened, membrane-bound sacs (cisternae) with two distinct faces of differing curvature — the cis (forming) face and the trans (maturing) face. (गॉल्जी उपकरण — परिपक्व सतह)

 

• As per the officially released SSC CGL answer key for this question, the maturing (trans) face of the Golgi apparatus is convex, facing towards the plasma membrane, from where processed vesicles are released.

 

• The Golgi apparatus receives proteins and lipids from the endoplasmic reticulum at its forming face, modifies and packages them as they pass through the stack, and dispatches them from the maturing face.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2, as per the official answer key.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Golgi apparatus was first described by the Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in 1898, after whom it is named.

 

• It plays a central role in the post-translational modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins, especially those destined for secretion or for lysosomes.

 

NOTE

 

• Spherical (Option 1): Does not describe either face of the Golgi apparatus.

 

• Bi-concave (Option 3): This shape describes structures such as red blood cells, not a face of the Golgi apparatus.

 

• Concave (Option 4): Some textbooks describe the trans/maturing face as concave and the cis/forming face as convex — the opposite pairing to the one used in the official key for this question; Option 2 is the answer per the released SSC key.

question: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded a reform association known as Brahmo Sabha which was later known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmo Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 in Calcutta, a reformist movement opposing idol worship and social evils like sati; it was later renamed and reorganised as the Brahmo Samaj, notably under Debendranath Tagore. (ब्रह्म सभा → ब्रह्म समाज — राजा राम मोहन राय)

 

• Ram Mohan Roy is widely regarded as the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" and played a key role in the abolition of Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.

 

• The Brahmo Samaj later saw a split, giving rise to the Adi Brahmo Samaj (Debendranath Tagore) and the Brahmo Samaj of India (Keshab Chandra Sen).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ram Mohan Roy also founded educational institutions and publications, including the Hindu College (with David Hare) and journals like Sambad Kaumudi.

 

• Other prominent 19th-century reform movements include the Arya Samaj (Swami Dayananda Saraswati, 1875) and the Prarthana Samaj (Bombay, 1867).

 

NOTE

 

• Dev Samaj (Option 1): A separate reform movement founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri in 1887, unrelated to the Brahmo Sabha.

 

• Arya Samaj (Option 2): Founded independently by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875, not a renaming of the Brahmo Sabha.

 

• Brahmo School (Option 3): Not the historical name that the Brahmo Sabha came to be known by.

question: ______ part of xylem tissue in plants stores food.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Xylem parenchyma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Xylem parenchyma consists of living cells that store food (starch, fat) and other reserve substances, and can also assist in short-distance lateral conduction of water. (जाइलम मृदूतक — भोजन भंडारण)

 

• Xylem tissue is composed of four elements: tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres, and xylem parenchyma — of these, only xylem parenchyma cells are living; the rest are dead at maturity.

 

• Tracheids and vessels are the main water-conducting elements, while xylem fibres provide mechanical strength/support to the plant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Xylem is a complex, permanent tissue primarily responsible for the conduction of water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant, and also provides mechanical support.

 

• The corresponding food-conducting tissue in plants is the phloem, which contains sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

 

NOTE

 

• Vessels (Option 1): Dead, tubular structures specialised for long-distance water conduction, not food storage.

 

• Xylem fibres (Option 2): Dead, elongated cells providing mechanical support, not food storage.

 

• Tracheids (Option 4): Dead, elongated cells involved in water conduction and support, not food storage.

question: Who among the following composers won the Grammy in 2015 for his album ‘Winds of Samsara' – a collaboration with South African flautist Wouter Kellerman?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ricky Kej.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ricky Kej, an Indian composer, won the Grammy Award for Best New Age Album in 2015 for his album 'Winds of Samsara', created in collaboration with South African flautist Wouter Kellerman. (रिकी केज — ग्रैमी अवार्ड 2015)

 

• 'Winds of Samsara' became the best-selling album in the New Age Album Billboard charts in the same year it was released.

 

• Ricky Kej is known for combining Indian classical and folk elements with world music, and is also active as an environmental activist and UNCCD Land Ambassador.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ricky Kej went on to win a second Grammy Award in 2022 (Best New Age Album) for the album 'Divine Tides', a collaboration with Stewart Copeland (drummer of The Police).

 

• He has also received honours such as the Global Peace Ambassador title and multiple environmental awards for his conservation work.

 

NOTE

 

• Mano Murthy (Option 1): A Kannada film music composer, not associated with this Grammy-winning album.

 

• Raghu Dixit (Option 2): An Indian folk-rock singer-composer, not associated with this Grammy-winning album.

 

• Subhashish Ghosh (Option 3): Not the composer associated with 'Winds of Samsara'.

question: In which of the following Indian states, Harappan cities have NOT been found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uttarakhand has not yielded any significant Harappan (Indus Valley Civilization) city sites; the Harappan Civilization's known extent does not reach into this hill state. (उत्तराखंड — हड़प्पा स्थल नहीं मिले)

 

• Gujarat hosts major Harappan sites such as Lothal, Dholavira, and Surkotada.

 

• Rajasthan hosts the site of Kalibangan, and Haryana hosts important sites such as Rakhigarhi, Banawali, and Bhirrana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rakhigarhi in Haryana is considered one of the largest Harappan sites discovered in the Indian subcontinent.

 

• Dholavira in Gujarat is renowned for its sophisticated water conservation and drainage system and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Has multiple confirmed Harappan sites, notably Lothal and Dholavira.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Has confirmed Harappan sites, notably Kalibangan.

 

• Haryana (Option 4): Has confirmed Harappan sites, notably Rakhigarhi and Banawali.

question: Burning of coal is an example of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is combination reaction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Burning of coal is a combination (combustion) reaction, in which carbon combines with oxygen to form carbon dioxide: C + O2 → CO2. (कोयले का जलना — संयोजन अभिक्रिया)

 

• A combination reaction is one in which two or more reactants combine to form a single product.

 

• Combustion of coal is also an exothermic reaction, releasing heat and light energy, which is why coal is used as a fuel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other everyday examples of combination reactions include the formation of water (2H2 + O2 → 2H2O) and rusting of iron (4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3, though this is slower).

 

• Coal is a major source of thermal power generation in India, though its combustion is also a significant contributor to greenhouse gas emissions.

 

NOTE

 

• decomposition reaction (Option 1): A reaction where one compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances — the opposite of what occurs when coal burns.

 

• double displacement reaction (Option 2): A reaction involving the exchange of ions between two compounds, not applicable to the burning of coal.

 

• displacement reaction (Option 4): A reaction where one element displaces another from a compound, not applicable to the burning of coal.

question: The foremost right among rights to freedom is ________.
option_1: Right to life and personal liberty
option_4: Right to freedom of speech and expression
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to life and personal liberty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Life and Personal Liberty, guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, is regarded as the foremost and most fundamental right among the rights to freedom, since all other freedoms presuppose the existence of life and liberty itself. (जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 21)

 

• Article 21 states: "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law."

 

• Over time, through judicial interpretation (notably in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, 1978), the scope of Article 21 has been expanded to include rights such as the right to a dignified life, privacy, clean environment, and livelihood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The broader Right to Freedom is covered under Articles 19 to 22 of the Constitution, including freedoms of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession (Article 19).

 

• Article 21 applies to "any person" (not just citizens), making it one of the most universally applicable fundamental rights in the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Preventive detention (Option 2): Covered under Article 22, this is a provision allowing detention without trial under specified safeguards — a limitation/exception mechanism, not a foremost right itself.

 

• Freedom to assemble (Option 3): One of the six freedoms under Article 19, but not regarded as the foremost right compared to the right to life itself.

 

• Right to freedom of speech and expression (Option 4): Also one of the six freedoms under Article 19, important but secondary to the foundational right to life and personal liberty.
